**Yes.** Under Section 31, the customer can terminate for convenience with **60 days' written notice**. The clause is mutual, so either party may terminate on the same terms.

> "Section 31. Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience by giving not less than sixty (60) days' written notice."

Two points to check:

- **The notice period is a minimum.** The clause says "not less than sixty (60) days," so a longer notice period is allowed, but 60 days is the shortest the customer can give.
- **The rest of the document is incomplete.** Sections 1 to 30 and 1 to 25 simply refer to the "master agreement" and contain no substantive terms. The master agreement itself was not provided, so it may contain other termination rights, notice requirements, or early-termination fees that could affect this answer. Review it before relying on Section 31.
